entities.summary: Pharaoh of the Eighteenth Dynasty (r. c. 1353–1336 BCE), born Amenhotep IV, who initiated a radical religious revolution — replacing the traditional Egyptian pantheon headed by Amun-Ra with exclusive worship of the Aten (the solar disk). He moved the capital from Thebes to a new city, Akhetaten (modern Amarna), closed Amun temples, and commissioned art in a distinctive naturalistic style. His "heresy" was reversed after his death, and his name was erased from king lists. Whether his Atenism constitutes true monotheism or monolatry remains debated. His wife Nefertiti and son Tutankhamun are among the most famous figures of antiquity.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Akhenaten's radical religious revolution led to a significant shift in Egyptian culture and politics, with his Atenism influencing subsequent pharaonic dynasties and leaving a lasting impact on the development of monotheistic thought. His legacy also includes the distinctive naturalistic art style that characterized Akhetaten.
